title: OAAP store list (oaap-store.json), list format 0.2 (RFC-0012)
$comment: Deliberately NOT additionalProperties:false, unlike oaap-app.schema.json. RFC-0012 §8.2 rule 1: a reader ignores what it does not know and never refuses because of it — and §8.3 reserves names (depends, provides, consumes, contributes, requires_platform, bundles, annotations, data_models, agents) that lists may already carry before this schema describes them. Strictness therefore lives in the authoring tools: the Store Editor and CI validate against this schema AND warn about unknown keys and unknown vocabulary values. A node in the field only reads.

store.$comment: 0.1 lists stay readable; every field added in 0.2 is optional.

id.$comment: Stable identity of the list, independent of its URL (RFC-0012 §4). Required for lists we ship, so they survive a move.

publisher.$comment: Shown verbatim next to the trust class as the origin (§3).

appId.$comment: Same shape as app.id in oaap-app.schema.json — the store resolves by this id (§3).

date.$comment: Release date of this version. The store computes the "neu" badge from it — RFC-0012 §1.1 explains why there is no stored 'new' flag.

relativePath.$comment: Resolved against the list URL. Absolute URLs are refused on purpose (§1.1): otherwise every node opening the store page would contact hosts nobody chose, announcing its existence and address for the sake of a thumbnail.

mustUnderstand.$comment: RFC-0012 §8.2 rule 2. Features a reader must understand to handle this entry correctly. A reader missing one refuses THIS entry with a clear message instead of installing something half-understood. Everything else may safely be ignored.

ref.$comment: Tag or commit. Without it the install takes whatever the default branch says at that moment (§5). Unpinned entries from non-platform sources are marked in the store; they are not refused (decision 3, 2026-08-09).

rel.$comment: Vocabulary: homepage, docs, source, demo, changelog, support, privacy, license. Unknown values are shown under "Weitere Links", not dropped (§1.1). 'demo' is a hosted demo to click through — an installable demo is a variant instead.

presentation.$comment: Editorial fields shared by apps and sets. RFC-0012 §1.3: the manifest is the truth about what a thing IS, the list about how it is presented and classified.

categories.$comment: Controlled vocabulary, several allowed (§1.2): business, productivity, documents, communication, media, monitoring, iot, automation, ai, development, security, storage-backup, infrastructure. Deliberately NOT an enum — a node must not refuse a list that uses a value newer than the node; unknown values are grouped under "Sonstiges" (decision 5, 2026-08-09). Authoring tools warn.

audience.$comment: Vocabulary: everyone, operator, developer, expert. 'expert' is marked and costs a confirmation at install — it is never a lock-out (decision 2026-08-08, relocated here from maturity).

tags.$comment: Free text by the publisher, used for SEARCH only — never for filters (§1.2). Curated remarks about a foreign app are a different mechanism, reserved as 'annotations' (§8.6).

type.$comment: RFC-0004: how it is packaged. Not to be confused with app_class, which says what it is.

homepage.$comment: Format 0.1. Read as a link with rel 'homepage'; new lists should use links[] instead.

profiles.$comment: RFC-0011: which node profiles this app is meant for (Studio: dev). The store filters and warns, it never refuses — the author describes, the operator decides.

roles.$comment: GENERATED from the manifest's route roles at publishing time (§1.3) — not a field anybody maintains. It lets the store answer "who can use this" without cloning the repository.

app_class.$comment: Vocabulary: frontend (has a user interface), service (backend only, used by other software). Decides whether an instance gets a launchpad tile. Data models are NOT a value here — they are their own artefact kind (kind: DataModel, §8.5).

maturity.$comment: Vocabulary: alpha, beta, preview, stable — how finished it is.

status.$comment: Vocabulary: active, deprecated (still installable, no longer recommended), archived (no longer offered, hidden by default). Whether it is still carried — a different question from maturity.

variants.$comment: Named alternatives of the SAME app, e.g. preview, demo (§1.1). The top-level version/released/package are the 'default' variant. Not the deploy channel production|test — that decides how an instance on THIS node may be redeployed.

set.$comment: An app set is a metapackage — RFC-0012 §8.5. It has no version, no package, no manifest and no health check, which is why it is a collection of its own rather than an app entry with empty fields. Installing a set installs its members as ordinary installs, each with its own source, trust class and confirmation; there is no transaction and no rollback. Do not confuse with 'bundles', which select services INSIDE one app.
